answer: No, they do not cover the same set of persons. The original definition of 'representative' was limited to an 'employee or an agent' of the investment adviser who renders investment advice on behalf of that adviser. The 2020-amended definition of 'persons associated with investment advice' is substantially broader: it extends to 'any member, partner, officer, director or employee or any sales staff' and further includes 'any person occupying a similar status or performing a similar function irrespective of the nature of association.' The Explanation also expressly deems all client-facing persons (e.g., sales staff, service relationship managers, client relationship managers) to be included, while excluding only persons who discharge clerical or office administrative functions with no client interface. Thus the amended definition captures a wider category of persons than the original 'representative' definition.

citations.quote:
Passage A:
Regulation 2(1)(r) (original, pre-2020): 'representative' means an employee or an agent of an investment adviser who renders investment advice on behalf of that investment adviser.

Passage B:
Regulation 2(1)(r) (as substituted w.e.f. 30-09-2020): 'persons associated with investment advice' shall mean any member, partner, officer, director or employee or any sales staff of such investment adviser including any person occupying a similar status or performing a similar function irrespective of the nature of association with the investment adviser who is engaged in providing investment advisory services to the clients of the investment adviser. Explanation — All client-facing persons such as sales staff, service relationship managers, client relationship managers, etc., by whatever name called shall be deemed to be persons associated with investment advice, but do not include persons who discharge clerical or office administrative functions where there is no client interface.

answer: No, they describe different types of professionals. An 'independent research analyst' is a person whose only business activity is research analysis or preparation and/or publication of a research report, meaning research is their sole business. A 'part-time research analyst' is an individual or partnership firm who provides research services for consideration but is simultaneously engaged in any other business activity or employment. The key distinction is that the independent research analyst has no other business activity, while the part-time research analyst does.
